newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas softer in Q3 on storage gas sale, J-Bloc.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas softer in Q3 on storage gas sale, J-Bloc.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market softened further on Monday in the third quarter, extending the sharp falls seen on Friday, but was relatively stable in other periods, traders and brokers said.

Q3 was weaker for three main reasons, dealers said. Transco announced at the end of last week that it would be issuing a tender for the disposal of around 82 million therms of Balancing Margins gas over the summer in a phased disposal; Enron and the J-Block co-venturers announced that they have settled their litigation over J-Block; and the Lennox oilfield in Liverpool Bay has restarted after a year long shutdown, which one player cited as a bearish factor in the gas market.
Several in the market said they had anticipated an announcement on J-Block. "The last bit of the jigsaw was the big sale on Friday," said a trader referring to heavy selling by Enron then.
Others agreed, with some saying the market had already factored in the J-Block news following Friday's sale.
"J-Block really happened on Friday," said one, and another added that "the fall today may be on the back of the storage position (the Balancing Margins sale) rather than J-Block."

Bids retreated after the J-Block announcement, with a trader saying "there was a stand-off after the announcement from the J-Block owners, as everybody said 'what does it mean to me?'." By the close the third quarter was heard bid at 10.30 pence against an offer at 10.35 pence, but no trade was heard done at these levels.

Further out the market was thin and relatively stable. But the prompt market was busy following a system buy of 16,654,485 kiloWatt hours (around 568,000 therms) at a system marginal price of 0.4651 p/kWh, or around 13.63 pence a therm.

The SAP on Sunday was 0.4647 p/kWh (around 13.62 pence a therm), with the 7-day average at 0.3789 p/kWh (11.10 pence a therm). As a result, within day prices moved up, with 12.90 pence a therm done, but day ahead prices were lower again, with deals done at both 11.70 and 11.75 pence at the NBP.

IPE futures were slightly off, but only a single deal was done for 25 lots and a futures broker said that the news headlines which had helped cause the weakness on Q3 on the OTC market had had little bearing on futures.
